ranked_facts.why: The presence of a mucosal fenestration with a visible hard, mineralized structure is more characteristic of a benign odontogenic tumor, such as a peripheral odontoma, than of a jaw exostosis or osteoma, which typically presents as a bony outgrowth without such a fenestration.

A discrete radiopaque lesion on a periapical radiograph is more indicative of a benign odontogenic tumor, such as a peripheral odontoma, which can appear as a well-defined radiopacity, than of a non-odontogenic calcified lesion, which may have a different radiographic appearance.
